shortDescription: American Eagle NYSE:AEO delivered better-than-expected results for the second quarter, beating on both the top- and bottom-line, with the company’s profit improving 34% year-over-year thanks to $196M in tariff refunds plus interest.Shares quickly reversed knee-jerk gains, however, and fell into the…

children: , beating on both the top- and bottom-line, with the company’s profit improving 34% year-over-year thanks to $196M in tariff refunds plus interest.

Shares quickly reversed knee-jerk gains, however, and fell into the red on approach to resistance at the 200-day moving average as gross margin excluding the benefit of tariffs was actually compressed year-over-year due to promotional pricing and rising supply chain costs.

nameplate brand saw a 1% decline in comparable store sales, while Aerie and OFFLINE realized a 19% surge in comparable store sales, resulting in a 25% increase in Aerie and OFFLINE revenue. Total comparable store sales increased 6%, up from -1% last year but just below the 6.47% estimate.

Total sales increased 9.4% to $1.4B versus $1.37B estimates, leading to an adjusted profit of $0.79 per share compared to $0.45 last year and $0.37 better than estimates. The per share amount, however, includes nearly $200M in tariff refunds.
For the third quarter, American Eagle
expects comparable sales to increase by mid-to-high single digits, no change to gross margin, and operating income to be between $110M and $115M.

For FY26, comparable sales are expected to increase by mid-single digits, gross margin improving, and operating income to be within a range of $540M and $550M from an earlier outlook of $390M and $410M.

title: American Eagle Outfitters Q2 profit, gross margin inflated by tariff refunds
